MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the next number in the pattern 11, 14, 17, 20, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 22
   B. 26
   C. 23
   D. 24

2. What is the next number in the pattern 10, 15, 20, 25, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 35
   B. 31
   C. 29
   D. 30

3. What is the 8th multiple of 7? (1 mark)
   A. 15
   B. 56
   C. 49
   D. 63

4. What is the 4th multiple of 9? (1 mark)
   A. 36
   B. 27
   C. 13
   D. 45

5. Work out 5,684 + 3,749. (1 mark)
   A. 9,333
   B. 9,443
   C. 8,323
   D. 9,433

6. A hen lays 21 eggs in a month. How many eggs do 16 hens lay in a month? (1 mark)
   A. 326 eggs
   B. 436 eggs
   C. 316 eggs
   D. 336 eggs

7. What is 15 × 40? (1 mark)
   A. 600
   B. 60
   C. 55
   D. 6,000

8. What is 25 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 125
   B. 250
   C. 25,000
   D. 2,500

9. What is 800 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 80
   C. 800
   D. 9

10. What is 79 ÷ 8? (1 mark)
   A. 8 remainder 15
   B. 9 remainder 7
   C. 9 remainder 8
   D. 10 remainder 7

11. Change 4 3/8 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 32/8
   B. 35/8
   C. 7/8
   D. 36/8

12. Ali writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 7/4
   B. 3/8
   C. 5/12
   D. 1 3/4

13. Write 2 25/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.225
   B. 2.25
   C. 22.5
   D. 2.025

14. Simplify 2c + 3d + 4c. (1 mark)
   A. 6c + 7d
   B. 6c + 3d
   C. 2c + 7d
   D. 9cd

15. Which expression shows "the cost of 6 books at b shillings each"? (1 mark)
   A. b − 6
   B. b ÷ 6
   C. 6 + b
   D. 6b

16. What is a quarter of a metre in centimetres? (1 mark)
   A. 250 cm
   B. 4 cm
   C. 14 cm
   D. 25 cm

17. A square has sides of 25 m. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 50 m
   B. 75 m
   C. 100 m
   D. 625 m

18. What is 1 m 35 cm + 2 m 85 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 20 cm
   B. 4 m 10 cm
   C. 4 m 20 cm
   D. 5 m 20 cm

19. Change 12 m to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 1,200 cm
   B. 12,000 cm
   C. 12 cm
   D. 120 cm

20. Rectangle P has 8 rows and 7 columns. Rectangle Q has 9 rows and 6 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle P
   B. Rectangle Q
   C. It cannot be told
   D. They are equal

21. A rectangle is made of 6 rows with 6 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 36 square units
   B. 42 square units
   C. 12 square units
   D. 24 square units

22. Which statement about a cube is true? (1 mark)
   A. Its length is double its width
   B. It has only 4 faces
   C. Its length, width and height are equal
   D. It has no corners

23. What is 1/2 L + 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 1 L
   B. 1 1/4 L
   C. 3/4 L
   D. 1/2 L

24. An electronic balance shows 2.5 kg. Which mass is this? (1 mark)
   A. 2 1/2 kg
   B. 25 kg
   C. 2 1/4 kg
   D. 2 3/4 kg

25. How many minutes are in 5 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 360 minutes
   B. 120 minutes
   C. 500 minutes
   D. 300 minutes

26. How many minutes are in 3 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 72 minutes
   B. 240 minutes
   C. 180 minutes
   D. 300 minutes

27. How many days are in 3 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 28 days
   B. 21 days
   C. 15 days
   D. 72 days

28. How many cents are in Ksh 25? (1 mark)
   A. 125 cents
   B. 25,000 cents
   C. 2,500 cents
   D. 250 cents

29. How can you test whether a corner is a right angle? (1 mark)
   A. Count its sides
   B. Weigh it
   C. Fit the corner of a folded piece of paper into it
   D. Measure its colour

30. A floor tile has four equal sides and four square corners. What shape is it? (1 mark)
   A. Oval
   B. Square
   C. Rectangle with unequal sides
   D. Triangle

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how the length of a shadow changes from morning to afternoon and explain how this can help us to estimate the time of day. (4 marks)

32. Complete the pattern 3, 6, 12, 24, ... with the next two numbers and state the rule. (3 marks)

33. Explain how you can use a beam balance to find the mass of a bag of sugar. (3 marks)

34. Rectangle P has 5 rows and 7 columns. Rectangle Q has 6 rows and 6 columns. Which has the bigger area and by how much? (4 marks)

35. A trip costs Ksh t for each pupil. Write an expression for the cost for 20 pupils and find the cost if t = 150. (3 marks)

36. A box is packed with cubes in layers. Each layer has 8 cubes along the length and 5 cubes across the width. There are 4 layers. (a) How many cubes are in one layer? (b) What is the volume of the packed cubes? (c) If 30 cubes are taken out, how many cubes are left? (5 marks)

37. Divide 450 by 100 and give the remainder. Explain what the remainder means. (4 marks)

38. Explain how multiplication can be used to check that 72 ÷ 6 = 12. (3 marks)

39. A stadium seats 9,000 people. During a match 6,450 seats are taken. How many seats are empty? (3 marks)

40. Share 96 metres of rope equally into pieces of 8 metres. How many pieces are there? (2 marks)

41. Achieng buys 3 packets of flour of 1/2 kg each and 2 packets of sugar of 1 kg each. Find the total mass. (3 marks)

42. A farmer has 95 eggs to pack into trays that each hold 6 eggs. (a) How many full trays are there and how many eggs are left over? (b) How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (5 marks)

43. Kip faces west and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? Explain. (3 marks)

44. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 2,000, 2,300, 2,600, 2,900. (3 marks)

45. Njeri had Ksh 5,000. She bought a school bag for Ksh 1,850. How much change did she get? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 23
   The rule is add 3. 20 + 3 = 23.

2. D — 30
   The rule is add 5. 25 + 5 = 30.

3. B — 56
   Multiply 7 × 8 = 56. It is the 8th multiple of 7.

4. A — 36
   Multiply 9 × 4 = 36. It is the 4th multiple of 9.

5. D — 9,433
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 5,684 + 3,749 = 9,433.

6. D — 336 eggs
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 336 eggs.

7. A — 600
   15 × 4 = 60, then × 10 gives 600.

8. D — 2,500
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 25 × 100 = 2,500.

9. A — 8
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 800 ÷ 100 = 8.

10. B — 9 remainder 7
   8 × 9 = 72 and 79 − 72 = 7. So 79 ÷ 8 = 9 remainder 7. Check: 9 × 8 + 7 = 79.

11. B — 35/8
   4 × 8 = 32 and 32 + 3 = 35. The denominator stays 8, so the answer is 35/8.

12. A — 7/4
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 7/4 is one whole or more.

13. B — 2.25
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 2 25/100 = 2.25.

14. B — 6c + 3d
   Only like terms can be joined. 2c + 3d + 4c = 6c + 3d.

15. D — 6b
   The key words tell us the operation. "the cost of 6 books at b shillings each" is written 6b.

16. D — 25 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: a quarter of a metre in centimetres is 25 cm.

17. C — 100 m
   A square has four equal sides. 25 + 25 + 25 + 25 = 100.

18. C — 4 m 20 cm
   Change to centimetres: 135 + 285 = 420 cm = 4 m 20 cm.

19. A — 1,200 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 12 × 100 = 1200. So the answer is 1,200 cm.

20. A — Rectangle P
   P = 8 × 7 = 56 and Q = 9 × 6 = 54. Rectangle P has the bigger area.

21. A — 36 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 6 × 6 = 36 square units.

22. C — Its length, width and height are equal
   A cube has 6 equal square faces, so its length, width and height are the same.

23. C — 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 1/2 L + 1/4 L = 3/4 L.

24. A — 2 1/2 kg
   0.5 is half, so 2.5 kg is 2 1/2 kg.

25. D — 300 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 5 × 60 = 300 minutes.

26. C — 180 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.

27. B — 21 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 3 × 7 = 21 days.

28. C — 2,500 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 25 = 25 × 100 = 2,500 cents.

29. C — Fit the corner of a folded piece of paper into it
   A folded paper corner is a right angle checker. If it fits exactly, the corner is a right angle.

30. B — Square
   Four equal sides and four right angles make a square.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: In the morning shadows are long, they get shorter towards midday when they are very short, and then get longer again in the afternoon. A very short shadow means it is about midday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for long in the morning, 1 mark for short at midday, 1 mark for long again in the afternoon, 1 mark for estimating time.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rule: multiply by 2. Next numbers: 48 and 96.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule, 1 mark for each correct number.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the sugar in one pan. Add known masses to the other pan until the beam is level. Add up the masses to find the mass of the sugar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for putting the sugar in a pan, 1 mark for adding known masses until level, 1 mark for adding the masses.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Q is bigger by 1 square unit.
   Working / marking points: P = 35 (1 mark); Q = 36 (1 mark); Q is bigger (1 mark); difference 1 (1 mark).

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20t. When t = 150, cost = 20 × 150 = Ksh 3,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 20t, 1 mark for replacing t by 150, 1 mark for Ksh 3,000.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 40 cubes (b) 160 cubes (c) 130 cubes
   Working / marking points: (a) 8 × 5 = 40 (1 mark); (b) 40 × 4 = 160 (2 marks); (c) 160 − 30 = 130 (2 marks).

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4 remainder 50. There are 4 whole hundreds in 450 and 50 is left over.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4, 1 mark for remainder 50, 2 marks for the explanation.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Multiply the answer by the divisor: 12 × 6 = 72. This gives the starting number, so the division is correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for multiplying the answer by the divisor, 1 mark for 12 × 6 = 72, 1 mark for the conclusion.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,550 seats
   Working / marking points: 9,000 − 6,450 with regrouping across zeros. 1 mark for the setup, 1 mark for regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: 12 pieces
   Working / marking points: 96 ÷ 8 = 12. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 kg (1 mark); 2 × 1 = 2 kg (1 mark); total 3 1/2 kg (1 mark).

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 15 full trays and 5 eggs left over (b) 16 trays
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 95 ÷ 6 = 15 remainder 5, 1 mark for stating both, 1 mark for the leftover eggs needing another tray, 1 mark for 16.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: North
   Working / marking points: Going clockwise the order is N, E, S, W and back to N (1 mark). West then a quarter turn clockwise gives north (1 mark). Answer north (1 mark).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3,200, 3,500, 3,800 (rule: add 300)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 3,150
   Working / marking points: 5,000 − 1,850 = 3,150. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the answer with Ksh.
